title: Snow
description: Snow is ice falling and settling: large flakes in backlight, a muffled world, tracks that record who passed. The air holds crystals you can size; the ground accumulates; contrast goes soft because the world has been covered.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Flakes cross a sodium lamp like slow sparks that do not burn. Shoulders collect white.
Footsteps write the path. Hush the world.
Silence becomes visible as reduced contrast and falling matter. Use it when winter must occupy both air and ground.
It is the wrong tool when you only need pale air without accumulation (Mist). It is the wrong tool when the falling matter is liquid (Rain).
Rain wets and mirrors; snow blankets and records tracks. Tiny fast specks against a day sky read as video noise.
Size the flakes and backlight them.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Put flakes in the air (practical or digital) large enough to read, and light them from behind or the side. Let accumulation sit on wool, hair, rails, and ground.
Keep a dark background for flakes to separate, or accept a white-on-white hush. Wind decides drift versus fall.
Prompt: falling snow around [Subject], large flakes in backlight, muffled world, tracks, winter silence you can see.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for a platform wait, a hunt, a small-town crime, a night street that should go quiet. Do not use it as white rain that never settles.
If shoulders stay dry and the pavement is only wet, you shot rain.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Rain streaks and mirrors. Mist hangs and does not accumulate as a blanket.
Blue Hour is a sky condition that often pairs with snow but is not weather. Dust Motes are indoor specks in a shaft.
Snow falls, lands, and stays.
MistSofter mystery than fog. Lyric, not monster.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Fargo lets snow be ground, air, and isolation. Let the Right One In uses falling flakes and muffled suburbs.
The Revenant puts bodies into falling and settled winter. Use accumulation and backlight, not a noise overlay.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Falling snow around [Subject], large flakes in backlight, muffled world, tracks, winter silence you can see. Name flake size, a lamp or sun behind them, accumulation on shoulders and ground, and tracks if anyone has walked.
For video, fall plus settle; no dry coats, no rain streaks.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Rain tinted white, or grain called snow. The tell: wet mirrors, no accumulation, specks too small to size.
The fix: large backlit flakes, settled white on surfaces, tracks, a hush in contrast.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Snow in film?
Snow is ice in the air and on the ground: backlit flakes, accumulation, tracks, a quieter contrast. It occupies volume and records passage.
Snow vs Rain
Rain is liquid: streaks, splashes, mirrors. Snow is crystal: drift, settle, blanket. If the street specularizes and coats stay dark, you are still in rain.
When should I use Snow?
Use it when winter should hush the world and leave tracks. Do not use it as white rain, and do not omit accumulation.
How do I prompt Snow for AI image or video?
Specify large backlit flakes and settled white. Example: falling snow around [Subject], large flakes in backlight, muffled world, tracks. Demand accumulation on wool and ground.
